description: Icon array and tree diagram of 1,000 people showing how the base rate, sensitivity, and specificity of a test determine the probability of disease given a positive result.

learningObjectives: Analyze how the prior probability, sensitivity, and specificity affect P(Disease | Positive) (Analyze)
Apply Bayes' theorem to calculate a posterior probability from its three inputs (Apply)
Explain base rate neglect using counts of true positives and false positives (Understand)
prerequisites: Conditional probability and the general multiplication rule

keyQuestions: How many positive tests come from people who are healthy?
What happens to the answer as the disease becomes more common?
commonMisconceptions: P(Disease | Positive) equals the sensitivity of the test
A highly accurate test cannot produce mostly false positives
The base rate does not matter once you have a test result
assessmentOpportunities: Student computes P(Disease | Positive) by hand for a new set of values and checks it with the MicroSim
Student explains the result using counts out of 1,000 people
Student identifies base rate neglect in a news story or advertisement
